title: Head CT
what: A CT scan shows your brain and skull bones in thin slices. It is fast, and usually no needle is needed.
why: After a head injury, if a stroke is suspected, for severe headaches, and to check the sinuses.
duration: usually 5 to 10 minutes in the room; the scan itself takes less than a minute
tell_doctor: If you are or could be pregnant
If your CT is with contrast: any allergy to iodine or contrast, and any kidney disease
If it is hard for you to lie still, or you fear tight spaces. The machine is open, but tell them ahead of time

prepare.title: Without contrast
prepare.text: No prep needed. You can eat and drink.

prepare.title: With contrast
prepare.text: You are usually asked not to eat for 3 to 4 hours. Water is fine. Sometimes you need a creatinine blood test. Check with your clinic.

prepare.title: Metal
prepare.text: Take off earrings, hair clips, glasses, dentures, and hearing aids.

bring: Past head CT and MRI scans
Your creatinine test result, if you were asked
steps: You lie on your back with your head in a soft holder
The table moves into a wide ring. Your head is inside, your body outside
Stay still while the machine takes pictures
If you have contrast, it goes into a vein and more pictures are taken
feel: It does not hurt. The machine makes noise
With contrast: a warm feeling and a metal taste. It passes in a minute
after: You can go back to your day straight away
After contrast, drink more water, unless your doctor said otherwise
The report is usually ready in a few hours or 1 to 2 days. In an emergency, right away
red_flags: A sudden, severe headache, weakness in an arm or leg, a drooping face, or trouble speaking: call emergency services right away
After contrast: itching, a rash, a swollen face, or trouble breathing. Tell the staff or call emergency services

faq.q: Which is better for the head, CT or MRI?
faq.a: CT is faster and better for injuries and bleeding. MRI shows brain tissue in more detail. Your doctor chooses based on the question.

faq.q: How much radiation is in a head CT?
faq.a: More than an x-ray, but the dose is set for the task. If a CT is needed for a medical reason, the benefit is greater than the risk.

faq.q: Why is a CT scan so fast?
faq.a: The X-ray tube and detectors spin around you more than once a second while the table moves smoothly. The whole body can be scanned in seconds; just keep still and hold your breath when asked.
